reason: This passage from Exodus 3-4 (the burning bush narrative) explicitly contradicts the notion of elite superiority. The text demonstrates: (1) God's deep concern for the suffering of ordinary people ('I have surely seen the affliction of my people...and have heard their cry'), (2) God's choice of Moses—an ordinary person with speech impediments—for leadership, based on divine calling rather than elite status, (3) God's affirmation that human capabilities transcend social position ('Who has made man's mouth...Is it not I, the Lord?'), and (4) inclusive leadership through the gathering and belief of the common elders of Israel. The narrative emphasizes divine power and compassion for the afflicted masses, not the inherent superiority of any elite class.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
